propositions: models_at_or_above with a non-ladder primary returns the full ladder instead of the primary alone, causing escalation to downgrade window and jump provider family
largest_window_tokens with a non-ladder primary returns the ladder maximum instead of the ladder minimum, overstating available context
prerequisite-coverage escalation at prerequisites.py:260-263 inherits the same defect when models_at_or_above returns an unlocated primary

The fix returns [model] for truthy-but-unlocated primaries in models_at_or_above and min(window) for the same case in largest_window_tokens, preserving single-criterion retry and conservative blocking
For a non-Anthropic model, escalation should stay on the operator's configured model and produce _too_big failure finding, not cross provider families
Back-compat: located Anthropic primaries and None-model defaults must preserve existing ladder-maximum and full-ladder behaviour
